content.text: {"title":"The Hill Picnic","premise":"Two children and a thoughtful donkey prepare a picnic on a windy hill for a guest who cannot climb it. They must discover what the guest needs, balance limited carrying space, and decide whether hospitality means bringing the hill down, carrying the picnic up, or making a clever shared arrangement at the hill’s foot.","cast_and_props":"Characters: Ada, an observant child who loves ambitious plans; Ben, a careful child who notices practical details; Moss, a strong but opinionated donkey with useful knowledge of paths and carrying comfort; Noor, the guest, an adult or older neighbor who cannot climb the hill but can help judge what would make the picnic feel welcoming. Places: hilltop, hillfoot, orchard path, small shelter. Props: two pannier baskets with limited capacity, picnic blanket, bread-and-fruit bundle, folding stool, rope, windbreak cloth, thermos, and a handcart. The handcart is usable only on suitable ground and requires cooperation.","kernels_and_interactions":"1. Ambition: Ada wants the picnic at the hilltop, increasing planning energy but risking overload. 2. Observation and mistaken belief: the children initially assume Noor only needs a seat, then learn through inspection or conversation that the difficult part may be the steep route, wind, or feeling left out. 3. Care and pride: Noor wants hospitality without being treated as helpless; Moss resists an uncomfortable or overloaded load. 4. Cooperation: characters can transfer supplies, divide the picnic, use the shelter, or pull the handcart together. Physical carrier scenes include carrying panniers, testing the path, setting a blanket, arranging a windbreak, and serving food.","seed_parameters":"Use rng from seed to vary causal conditions: guest need (cannot climb because of breath, knee, or unstable footing); hill condition (dry and rolling, muddy, or windy); Moss’s carrying comfort and pannier capacity; available cart condition (smooth wheels or one wheel needing adjustment); Noor’s preferred hospitality (quiet shelter, view of the hilltop, or participation in preparing food). Seed must alter which plans are physically viable, not merely names. Initialize all people, places, props, ownership, locations, capacities, weights, weather/path states, needs, memes, and knowledge slots. Initialize built-in meme and knowledge keys for curiosity, care, ambition, observations, and communicated beliefs.","candidate_scenes":"1. inspect_path: Ada or Ben examines the hill route when physically present, learning slope or mud conditions. 2. ask_noor: a child asks Noor what makes the hill difficult and records the answer as knowledge. 3. inspect_baskets: Ben checks capacity and discovers whether the original menu fits. 4. tell_moss_plan: a child explains the intended load to Moss after learning it. 5. moss_rejects_overload: Moss refuses an uncomfortable load, changing the children’s plan and raising attention to his needs. 6. choose_menu: the children reduce or divide supplies based on capacity and Noor’s preference. 7. repair_cart: Ben and Moss adjust a loose cart wheel if the cart is available and repairable. 8. transfer_supplies: the keeper-like caretaker or Moss transfers ownership of selected picnic items to the children, respecting care and capacity. 9. pull_cart_to_foot: characters move supplies along a usable lower path with the cart. 10. carry_panniers_up: Moss and a child carry a safe load up the hill when slope and comfort permit. 11. set_windbreak: the children and Noor arrange cloth near the hillfoot or summit, physically reducing wind. 12. arrange_shelter_picnic: Noor and the children prepare a welcoming picnic at the hillfoot shelter. 13. prepare_split_picnic: one group takes a small view portion uphill while Noor joins a substantial shared portion below, linked by a food or message transfer. 14. invite_moss_rest: the children give Moss water and a rest space, making continued cooperation possible. 15. serve_and_share: characters serve the final arrangement only when food, place, and Noor’s desired participation align. Scenes should be reusable and guarded by physical state, location, ownership, capacity, and learned knowledge rather than route IDs.","constraints":"Use 2–4 interacting kernels and at least one built-in kernel such as observe, tell, or transfer. Use 8–16 scenes, with roughly 5–10 selected events per run. Every scene needs a physical carrier and must cause a non-no-op state change. Keep the world grounded: no impossible lifting, teleporting, or magically flattening terrain. Rules should prevent overloaded panniers, unsafe cart use, missing food, contradictory ownership, and serving before the picnic is arranged. Guard deliberate choices with knowledge obtained by observation or communication. The goal should require Noor to be included in a completed picnic arrangement, with either a hilltop, hillfoot, or split arrangement reachable. Ensure at least two endings: a successful hilltop picnic when route, cart, and carrying conditions permit; and a welcoming hillfoot or split picnic when Noor’s needs, weather, or capacity make the original plan unsuitable. A third variation may end with a sheltered orchard picnic if the hill becomes too windy.","different_endings":"Ending A: Noor shares food at the hilltop, shown by the blanket spread, safe supplies present, and Moss resting nearby after a manageable climb. Ending B: the group holds a rich hillfoot picnic under the shelter, with a view token such as a hilltop sketch or bell message proving the hill was included without forcing Noor to climb. Ending C: a split picnic lets Noor eat with the children at the hillfoot while a small view basket and shared message connect to a hilltop portion; the concrete final image is two matching cups or plates linked by the carried cloth napkin. The final arrangement must follow actual state and should not claim that Noor climbed, the cart worked, or the weather calmed unless corresponding scenes caused it."}
